guidance.overview: A structured 30-minute discovery agenda that ensures all SPIN categories are covered and key qualification gaps are surfaced before the meeting ends.

segments.name: Introductions and meeting goal
segments.desired_outcome: Both parties agree on what a successful meeting looks like.
segments.notes: State the meeting objective out loud and get the customer to confirm or adjust it.

segments.name: Situation
segments.desired_outcome: Confirm current-state facts: environment, team, systems in use.
segments.notes: Reference any CRM context you already have to avoid re-asking known facts.

segments.name: Problem and Implication
segments.desired_outcome: Customer has described their key pain points and acknowledged the business impact.
segments.notes: Probe for consequences — operational, financial, compliance, or reputational. Do not rush to solutions.

segments.name: Need-Payoff and success criteria
segments.desired_outcome: Customer has articulated what success looks like in their own words.
segments.notes: Ask what a solution would enable, not what product they want.

segments.name: Qualification gaps
segments.desired_outcome: Budget authority, decision process, and timeline are partially understood or explicitly flagged as unknown.
segments.notes: Cover the unknowns list from the opportunity record. Do not pressure; frame as 'to help us prepare the right next step'.

segments.name: Recap and next steps
segments.desired_outcome: Both parties leave with a clear, agreed next action and owner.
segments.notes: Summarise what you heard, confirm any commitments, and propose a specific next step.

guidance.scaling_rule: For meetings longer than 30 minutes, extend Problem/Implication and Need-Payoff proportionally. For shorter meetings, compress Situation and skip Qualification gaps if necessary — protect the Implication time.
tips: Send a brief agenda to the customer in advance so they arrive prepared.
Keep a visible timer to avoid overrunning Situation questions.
If the customer steers to solutions early, acknowledge it and park it: 'That is worth exploring — let me make a note and we will come back to it.'
